newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIAN CERA TO GIVE UP ONE PRIMARY DEALERSHIP.
newsitem.headline: BELGIAN CERA TO GIVE UP ONE PRIMARY DEALERSHIP.

text.p: Belgian Cera Bank or its future unit Banque Indosuez Belgium will give up its status as primary dealer of Belgian state debt when Cera's takeover of Indosuez Belgium becomes effective in April-May, Cera said on Wednesday.
"One can wonder whether it is necessary that both should remain primary dealer," Cera Bank chief executive officer Willy Breesch told Reuters in an interview.
Breesch also said Indosuez will become a seperate, independent unit of Cera Bank and will get a new name.
Cera said in December it had struck a basic deal with French Indosuez to buy 80 percent of Indosuez Belgium. Breesch declined to say how much Cera would pay for Indosuez Belgium.

Indosuez Belgium, in which Indosuez France will keep a 20 percent stake, is a small bank specialised in capital markets, corporate finance, investment banking and asset management. It had assets worth 225 billion francs at the end of 1995.
Cera is Belgium's sixth-largest bank, with assets totalling 1,241 billion at the end of 1995. It specialises in retail banking, banking for small and medium-size companies and agricultural credits.

There are currently 15 primary dealers of Belgian state debt, whose task is to make markets in Belgian linear bonds and Treasury bills. In exchange they can participate in the Treasury's non-competitive auctions and also have a privileged relation with the central bank.
Banque Internationale a Luxembourg also gave up its Belgian primary dealer status after it was acquired by Belgian Credit Communal/Gemeentekrediet in the early nineties.
Breesch said that Cera's new unit will continue to focus on financial markets and added it will have a large operational independence.
He also confirmed that Cera's 100 percent brokerage unit Nedee & Cie was in talks with fellow brokerage Mignon, Hanart, Declerck with a view to a cooperation agreement.
The expansion into financial services will allow Cera (still mainly known as an agricultural bank) to hoist itself up into the circle of large retail banks with a full range of banking services.
"Compared to Belgium's large banks, we were lagging behind in professional activities,' he said.
Breesch said Cera would have no problem financing the Indosuez takeover from its own funds and added that he expected the unit to be consolidated in Cera's 1997 full-year accounts.
He also said his bank was still on the lookout for other opportunities in the sector.
"We are not actively looking for other acquisitions, but when an opportunity presents itself, we will certainly consider it," he said.
Breesch, who is also chairman of the Belgian Banking Association, has been Cera chief executive since January 1, 1994. -- Geert De Clercq, Brussels Newsroom +32 2 287 6813
